newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Strike threat at Hungary MOL's main refinery.
newsitem.headline: Strike threat at Hungary MOL's main refinery.

text.p: Hungarian oil and gas producer MOL could face a pay strike by employees at its Szazhalombatta refinery just outside Budapest.
Hungary's Oil Industry Trade Union is claiming an immediate 30 percent wage increase, as against 15 percent offered by the company from next July, the daily Nepszabadsag reported on Wednesday.
Union leader Barnabas Hajzer said current talks with employers were inconclusive and further deadlock could lead to strike action.
"If further talks do not result in agreement the union will decide on the formation of a strike committee on January 10," he said, adding that workers would walk out next week.
He said signatures of 51 percent of members necessary to call a strike had already been collected.
Hajzer added that his union could not accept an increase less than the national average in view of the company's plan to cut MOL's workforce by up to 1,600 this year.
MOL company officials were unavailable for comment.
Inflation in Hungary currently stands at around 23 percent.
MOL shares rose 155 on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday to end at 2,355 forints. On Wednesday they rose again, touching a high of 2,465 before retreating slightly.
